newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - April 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - April 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

A national conference on Chittagong Hill Tracts on Friday demanded a permanent solution to the long-standing crisis in the region on the basis of equal rights of both tribal and Bangalee people living there.
The government is actively considering raising the price of fertiliser to reduce subsidies.
The Health and Population Sector Strategy report has said that 90 percent of Bangladeshi children are malnourished.
Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) chief Begum Khaleda Zia on Friday demanded an immediate appointment of a judge of the supreme court as Chief Election Comissioner.
Three rebel leaders of the Jatiya Party of former President Hussain Mohammad Ershad on Friday decided to call the party's council meeting, auguring a formal split.
Bangladesh on Friday strongly deplored the Israeli action to change the demographic structure as well as legal and physical character of the holy city of Jerusalem.
Bangladesh Sugar and Food Industries Corporation (BSFIC) plans to import 0.15 million tonnes of sugar to meet the country's requirement and keep the sugar price stable in the market.
Bangladesh is heading towards a dramatic demographic transition with sharp fall in fertility and mortality rates, a recent report of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said.
